title: Shared workspaces, meeting areas and handover
intro: Coordinate shared workstations, meetings, circulation and services, then issue an installation and handover record tied to users and approved references.

sections.title: Map work modes and adjacency
sections.text: Record focus, calls, collaboration and shared storage needs by group. Map adjacency and simultaneous chair/circulation states. A partition’s appearance does not establish acoustic or privacy performance; route acoustic, access and exit requirements to the relevant review.
sections.caption: Adjacency follows tasks and use states.

sections.title: Test meetings, setup and changeover
sections.text: Test the meeting, reconfiguration and maintenance states with participants, display, door and equipment. Review sight lines, tool access and leaving seats. Added chairs require a new layout/movement check, not simply filling the table perimeter.
sections.caption: Meeting and changeover are distinct use states.

sections.title: Create a traceable handover record
sections.text: Code workstations, meeting groups and storage against products and drawing revisions. Record quantities, locations, acceptance, defects and available care/warranty information. 6 stations plus 2 meeting groups are 8 functional groups, not 8 furniture pieces; itemize components. Close defects with reinspection evidence and provide relevant user orientation.
sections.caption: Functional groups and physical pieces are different counts.

example.title: Worked case and decision
example.text: Six stations fit with chairs tucked in, but two pulled-out chairs block shared storage. Revise storage or station positions, retest the state and update the referenced drawing before procurement.
example.decision: Decision: validate shared use before fixing quantities and locations.

quiz.question: Do 6 workstations and 2 meeting groups mean exactly 8 furniture pieces?
quiz.explanation: A functional group may contain several physical items.

assignment.prompt: Submit a shared-office layout/use states, group/component schedule, installation plan and defect/reinspection card.

faq.question: Does a tall partition prove acoustic privacy?
faq.answer: No. Performance needs appropriate evidence and project-specific review, not appearance alone.
